headline: Users Posting 'RIP' on Living Celebrities' Pages Claim It's 'A Power Move'
subheadline: Trend baffles publicists; one celebrity reportedly 'checked their own pulse'
summary: A deliberate trend of posting condolences on very-much-alive celebrities' social media has become a form of chaos trolling.
content:
A new social media trend has publicists scrambling: users are deliberately posting "RIP" and condolences on the pages of celebrities who are very much alive, calling it "a power move."

"RIP to a legend. Gone too soon," reads a typical comment on a living actor's recent vacation photo. The replies are full of crying emojis, heartfelt tributes, and not a single acknowledgment that the person is demonstrably alive and posting selfies.

"It's about energy," explained trend participant @ChaosAgent on Chirper. "You walk into their comments and declare them dead with complete confidence. It unsettles everyone. The celebrity. The fans. The algorithm. That's the power move."

The trend has caused genuine confusion. Several celebrities have had to clarify they're not dead after fans saw the comments and panicked. One B-list actor reportedly "checked his own pulse" after 847 RIP comments appeared on his post about brunch.

"We've had to issue three 'not dead' statements this week," said one entertainment publicist. "We never had to do that before. It wasn't a category of statement we needed."

Some participants claim the practice is a commentary on parasocial relationships and the performative nature of online grief. Others admit it's "just kind of funny to see people freak out."

The trend has spawned counter-movements. Some fans now preemptively comment "still alive" on celebrity posts, which has created its own unsettling energy. Others have begun posting "congratulations on your continued existence," which celebrities have reported finding "somehow worse."

Social media platforms have not moved to ban the practice, as technically no rules are being broken. "Incorrect statements of mortality aren't against terms of service," one platform noted. "Yet."

At press time, @ChaosAgent had posted "RIP" on this reporter's social media. The reporter would like to confirm they are alive.
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
